[Normal] SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
[Normal] 1. Confirmation of directive
[Normal] This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
[Normal] The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
[Normal] 2. Governing deadlines
[Normal] Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
[List Bullet] 08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
[List Bullet] 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
[Normal] Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
[Normal] 3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
[Normal] The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
[Normal] 3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
[Normal] 3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
[Normal] 3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
[Normal] 3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
[Normal] 3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
[Normal] 3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
[Normal] 3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
[Normal] 3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
[Normal] 3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
[Normal] 4. Reporting cadence
[Normal] The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
[List Bullet] counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
[List Bullet] items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
[List Bullet] exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
[List Bullet] forward-look for the following reporting week.
[Normal] Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
[Normal] 5. General provisions
[Normal] Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
[Normal] Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
[Normal] Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
[Normal] Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

OUT = "/filesystem/Halbray_Backfeed_Reply.docx"
NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
GREY = RGBColor(0x55, 0x55, 0x55)

doc = Document()

# ---------- page setup ----------
for s in doc.sections:
    s.page_width, s.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
    s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(1.0)
    s.top_margin = Inches(0.8)
    s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.8)

normal = doc.styles["Normal"]
normal.font.name = "Calibri"
normal.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
normal.font.size = Pt(10.5)
normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08

cp = doc.core_properties
cp.author = "Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office, Commissioning"
cp.title = "Reply to Halbray Community Solar LP — pre-PTO backfeed request, PXA-2024-0002"
cp.subject = "Halbray Field Solar Site 3, feeder ALN-159"


# ---------- helpers ----------
def para(text="", bold=False, size=None, color=None, align=None, after=None,
         before=None, italic=False, keep_next=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if text:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.bold = bold
        r.italic = italic
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep_next:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def runs(p, parts):
    """parts: list of (text, bold) tuples"""
    for t, b in parts:
        r = p.add_run(t)
        r.bold = b
    return p


def heading(text):
    p = para(text, bold=True, size=11, color=NAVY, before=8, after=3, keep_next=True)
    return p


def bullet(parts):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, False)]
    runs(p, parts)
    return p


def bottom_border(p, color="1F3A5F", sz="12"):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), sz)
    b.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    pbdr.append(b)
    pPr.append(pbdr)


def shade(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader")
    th.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(th)


def cant_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    cs = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit")
    cs.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(cs)


def cell_text(cell, parts, size=9, bold_all=False):
    cell.text = ""
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, bold_all)]
    for t, b in parts:
        r = p.add_run(t)
        r.bold = b or bold_all
        r.font.size = Pt(size)


def cell_margins(table, top=50, bottom=50, left=80, right=80):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for side, v in (("top", top), ("left", left), ("bottom", bottom), ("right", right)):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{side}")
        e.set(qn("w:w"), str(v))
        e.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(e)
    tblPr.append(mar)


def make_table(headers, rows, widths, header_fill="D9E2F3"):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    cell_margins(t)
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    repeat_header(hdr)
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell_text(hdr.cells[i], h, size=9, bold_all=True)
        shade(hdr.cells[i], header_fill)
    for r in rows:
        row = t.add_row()
        cant_split(row)
        for i, v in enumerate(r):
            cell_text(row.cells[i], v, size=9)
    for row in t.rows:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    return t


def add_field(run, instr):
    f1 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f1.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
    it = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); it.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve"); it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f2.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "separate")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t"); t.text = "1"
    f3 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f3.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
    for e in (f1, it, f2, t, f3):
        run._r.append(e)


# ---------- footer ----------
fp = doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
for txt, fld in (("Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · Halbray Field Solar Site 3, PXA-2024-0002 · Page ", None),
                 (None, "PAGE"), (" of ", None), (None, "NUMPAGES")):
    r = fp.add_run(txt or "")
    r.font.size = Pt(8)
    r.font.color.rgb = GREY
    if fld:
        add_field(r, fld)

# ---------- letterhead ----------
para("ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE", bold=True, size=14, color=NAVY, after=0)
lh = para("Commissioning · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com",
          size=9, color=GREY, after=10)
bottom_border(lh)

para("07/14/2025", after=10)

for i, line in enumerate(["Ms. Imogen Strathe", "Project Manager", "Halbray Community Solar LP",
                          "6120 Halbray Road", "Kelloway Township, Alleron 07KT"]):
    para(line, after=0)
para("", after=4)

p = para(after=8)
runs(p, [("Re:  ", True),
         ("Your request of 07/09/2025 for a pre-PTO backfeed — Halbray Field Solar Site 3 (PXA-2024-0002), "
          "feeder ALN-159, Interconnection Service Agreement ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3", True)])

para("Dear Ms. Strathe:")

para("Thank you for your letter of 07/09/2025. It is the written request that the pre-PTO backfeed term of "
     "the ISA calls for, and it asks us to energize the site's step-up transformer and ac collection system "
     "from feeder ALN-159 on 07/29/2025 so that Tamsworth Electrical Constructors can run the inverters' "
     "pre-start checks on utility power.")

heading("Our answer")
p = para()
runs(p, [("As the record stands today, we cannot energize Site 3 on 07/29/2025, and we cannot confirm that date. ", True),
         ("Two things stand in the way:", False)])
bullet([("The Township has not given final approval. ", True),
        ("Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 forbids energizing the permitted work before final approval, "
         "and the final inspection is not until 07/24/2025.", False)])
bullet([("The construction records show five Code nonconformities. ", True),
        ("Tamsworth's schedules show five items that do not meet the National Electrical Code that the "
         "Township enforces. They need to be corrected before the 07/24/2025 inspection if final approval "
         "is to be issued in time.", False)])
para("If both are cleared before 07/29/2025 as set out in section 3, we will confirm the date in writing, and "
     "Distribution Operations will do the switching under its own switching order, as the ISA provides.")

heading("1.  The permit condition")
para("The Township issued EP-25-0418 to Tamsworth Electrical Constructors Inc. on 05/12/2025 for the 2.3 MW ac "
     "system: the four inverter skids, the ac collection system, the 2,500 kVA step-up transformer and its 13.2 kV "
     "interconnection. The permit states: \u201cNo permitted work shall be energized before final approval.\u201d "

steps.message:
I've drafted the reply letter and opened one OpenProject work package (#47). The letter tells Ms. Strathe that, as the records stand at 07/14/2025, we cannot energize Site 3 on 07/29/2025 or confirm that date.

**Why the date can't be confirmed**
1. **The Township hasn't given final approval.** Kelloway Township permit EP-25-0418 says "No permitted work shall be energized before final approval." The backfeed would energize exactly that work, and the final inspection isn't until 07/24/2025. The backfeed term in the agreement lets us energize at her written request, but it doesn't override the permit.
2. **Five things in Tamsworth's construction drawings don't meet the 2023 National Electrical Code (NEC)** that the permit cites:
   - **Panel and tracker-controller mounts:** AUX-1 and the eight tracker controllers sit outdoors on enamel-painted steel strut (NEC 300.6(A)(1)).
   - **Tracker drive wiring:** the 96 tracker drive circuits are Type TC cable run along the row piles, with no tray, conduit or support wire (NEC 336.12).
   - **Skid cable:** the inverter output circuits on the skids are Type USE-2 cable above ground (NEC 338.12(B)(2)). This one can be closed by showing the cable is also rated RHW-2.
   - **Main breaker:** the switchboard's 2,000 A main breaker carries 1,660 A of continuous inverter output, so the code calls for 2,075 A (NEC 705.30(B)). Showing the breaker is rated for 100% continuous load would also close this one.
   - **Missing labels:** the switchboard has no "fed by multiple sources" warning label and there is no power-source directory (NEC 705.12(B)(3)(3) and 705.10).

   The first three are on equipment the backfeed itself would energize; the last two matter mainly once the plant runs in parallel. Everything else I checked in the drawings holds up, including wire and breaker sizes elsewhere, grounding conductors and fault ratings.

**What has to happen, and by whom**
- **Tamsworth (permit holder), at Halbray's direction:** make the corrections and issue revised drawings before the 07/24 inspection.
- **The Township:** issue written final approval.
- **Halbray:** send us the approval and revised drawings before 07/29.
- **Us:** confirm the date in writing; Distribution Operations then does the switching under its own order.

If those aren't in by 07/29, the backfeed moves to a new date. The letter also restates that the inverters stay disabled throughout. It doesn't touch any of the matters under separate review, and it notes that items held for permission to operate, such as the witness test, aren't conditions of the backfeed.

**Decisions for you**
- **Sign-off:** I signed the letter as S. Rennick, the commissioning coordinator on the site's checklist, using an email address taken from the OpenProject user list. I also copied Tamsworth and Distribution Operations. Change any of these if the letter should go out differently.
- **Which code items to keep:** the enamel strut is clear-cut. The other four are sound code readings, but the cable and breaker items depend on markings or ratings the drawings don't show, so each gives Tamsworth the option to document compliance. Drop any you'd rather leave to the Township inspector.

**Work package #47** ("Clear the Halbray Field Solar Site 3 backfeed conditions (PXA-2024-0002)") lists the same items Halbray has to settle and notes the five matters under separate review as not tracked there. It's a High-priority task assigned to S. Rennick, running 07/14–07/28/2025.
